features.source: The Aleut people of the Aleutian Islands and Alaska Peninsula, whose self-name is Unangax̂. The -7000 start is a regional-continuity estimate: the Aleutian archaeological record documents ancestors of the Unangax̂ by about 9000 years ago, not a fixed early political boundary. Their island communities were autonomous; the Russian fur trade profoundly disrupted them after 1741 without ending Aleut life or identity.
